item: C1: regularized energy-dependent matrix field M_delta(B) = c lim_R int_{-R}^{R} (f(K^2 - 2sB + s^2) - f(s^2) I) ds on the Riccati variable B, its primitive J (dJ = -tr(M dB)), and the rank-one comparison M(B) = aa^T => a^T(K^2 - B^2)a >= |a|^{2q} (262-S Sec. 3-4)
lean_status_why: The field, its primitive, the commuting-data values, the boundary values and the rank-one comparison are Lean definitions and theorems with the paper's exact formulas (MatrixOrder.lean:16-56), and the comparator target depends on them through finite_action_upper_test; the Lean version is if anything more general (any complex Hermitian C in place of K^2).
lean_gaps: GENERALIZATION (not a weakening): the core development is for hermitianField sigma delta C B with an arbitrary complex Hermitian C (quadraticMatrix C B s = s^2 I + C - 2sB) and complex Hermitian B; the rank-one comparison is proved at that generality (rankone_hermitian_comparison) and transferred to the real field with C = K^2 by complexification (complexify_matrixField, source_rankone_comparison). The paper states everything for real symmetric B and diagonal K.

Definition: matrixField is Filter.limUnder of the symmetric-cutoff truncatedField (junk value if no limit); convergence is proved (hermitianField_cutoff_limit) for sigma < 1, delta > 0 via the paired s/-s integrand, which is absolutely integrable. Matches the paper's "symmetric cutoff is part of the definition".

Gradient route: the paper proves dJ = -tr(M dB) by a closed-curve argument with potentials -(1/2s) tr F(X_s(B)); Lean builds an explicit potential (pairedTracePotential / hermitianPotential with secondPrimitive) and proves HasFDerivAt directly. Same content, different proof.
The Prop wrapper RankOneClaim and its proof rankOneClaim are not in the comparator DAG; the DAG uses source_rankone_comparison directly (cosmetic).

The paper's Thm 2.1 (H^1_0 action inequality) is the unproved Prop ActionClaim in Lean; the field is consumed by finite_action_upper_test for continuous amplitudes with derivatives, which suffices for the comparator. This is a gap in the surrounding theorem, not in the item.
Only the scalar paper (262-S) is formalized. 262-M's use of the field (N = M_delta + delta^sigma) and C2 are not in Lean.
The field is only meaningful for 0 < sigma < 1 (all lemmas assume it); at sigma >= 1 the Lean fieldNormalization evaluates to 0 by the Bochner-integral convention.
Checked at text level only (no lake build, no comparator run), per orchestrator instruction; dependency chain from data/items/262_lean.json (extractor v3).

lean_source.name: OAI.SharpLiebThirring.regularizedPrimitive
OAI.SharpLiebThirring.fieldNormalization
lean_source.text:
def fieldNormalization (σ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  σ / ∫ s : ℝ, (1 + s ^ 2) ^ (σ - 3 / 2)

lean_source.name: OAI.SharpLiebThirring.scalarMu
OAI.SharpLiebThirring.matrixX
OAI.SharpLiebThirring.truncatedField
lean_source.text:
/-- The symmetric cutoff is part of the definition, not replaced
by a potentially non-absolutely-convergent whole-line Bochner integral. -/
def truncatedField (σ δ : ℝ) (k : Fin N → ℝ) (B : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℝ)
    (R : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℝ :=
  fieldNormalization σ • ∫ s in (-R)..R,
    cfc (regularizedPrimitive σ δ) (matrixX k B s) -
      regularizedPrimitive σ δ (s ^ 2) • 1

lean_source.name: OAI.SharpLiebThirring.matrixField
lean_source.text:
/-- The symmetric-cutoff limit, whose convergence and local regularity are proved below. -/
def matrixField (σ δ : ℝ) (k : Fin N → ℝ) (B : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℝ) :
    Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℝ :=
  Filter.limUnder Filter.atTop (truncatedField σ δ k B)

lean_source.name: OAI.SharpLiebThirring.fieldPrimitive
lean_source.text:
def fieldPrimitive (σ δ : ℝ) (k : Fin N → ℝ) (B : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℝ) : ℝ :=
  -(∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, Matrix.trace (B * matrixField σ δ k (t • B)))

lean_source.name: OAI.SharpLiebThirring.RankOneClaim
lean_source.text:
/-- The rank-one comparison for the symmetric-cutoff matrix field. -/
def RankOneClaim : Prop :=
  ∀ (σ δ : ℝ) (k : Fin N → ℝ) (B : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℝ) (a : Fin N → ℝ),
    0 < σ → σ < 1 → 0 < δ → (∀ i, 0 < k i) → B.IsHermitian →
    matrixField σ δ k B = Matrix.vecMulVec a a →
    (∑ i, a i * ((Matrix.diagonal (fun i ↦ (k i) ^ 2) - B ^ 2) *ᵥ a) i) ≥
      (∑ i, (a i) ^ 2) ^ (1 + 1 / σ)

lean_source.name: OAI.SharpLiebThirring.MatrixProof.quadraticMatrix
lean_source.text:
def quadraticMatrix (C B : Matrix n n ℂ) (s : ℝ) : Matrix n n ℂ :=
  s ^ 2 • 1 + (C - (2 * s) • B)

lean_source.name: OAI.SharpLiebThirring.MatrixProof.hermitianField
lean_source.text:
def hermitianField (σ δ : ℝ) (C B : Matrix n n ℂ) : Matrix n n ℂ :=
  (fieldNormalization σ / 2) • ∫ s : ℝ, pairedFieldIntegrand σ δ C B s

lean_source.name: OAI.SharpLiebThirring.MatrixProof.hermitianField_cutoff_limit
lean_source.text:
lemma hermitianField_cutoff_limit {σ δ : ℝ} (hσ : σ < 1) (hδ : 0 < δ)
    {C B : Matrix n n ℂ} (hC : C.IsHermitian) (hB : B.IsHermitian) :
    Tendsto (fun R : ℝ ↦ fieldNormalization σ • ∫ s in -R..R, fieldIntegrand σ δ C B s)
      atTop (𝓝 (hermitianField σ δ C B))

lean_source.name: OAI.SharpLiebThirring.MatrixProof.hermitianPotential_hasFDerivAt
lean_source.kind: lemma (gradient property, complex Hermitian, general C)
lean_source.text:
lemma hermitianPotential_hasFDerivAt {σ δ : ℝ} (hσ : σ < 1) (hδ : 0 < δ)
    (C B : selfAdjoint (Matrix n n ℂ)) :
    HasFDerivAt (hermitianPotential σ δ C)
      (traceGradientMap (hermitianField σ δ C B)) B

lean_source.name: OAI.SharpLiebThirring.MatrixProof.fieldPrimitive_path_derivative
lean_source.text:
lemma fieldPrimitive_path_derivative {σ δ : ℝ} (hσ : σ < 1) (hδ : 0 < δ)
    (k : Fin N → ℝ) {B : ℝ → selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℝ)}
    {B' : selfAdjoint (Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℝ)} {x : ℝ} (hB : HasDerivAt B B' x) :
    HasDerivAt (fun x ↦ fieldPrimitive σ δ k (B x))
      (-trace (matrixField σ δ k (B x) * (B' : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℝ))) x

lean_source.name: OAI.SharpLiebThirring.MatrixProof.matrixField_diagonal
lean_source.text:
lemma matrixField_diagonal {N : ℕ} {σ δ : ℝ} (hσ : σ < 1) (hδ : 0 < δ)
    (k b : Fin N → ℝ) :
    matrixField σ δ k (diagonal b) = diagonal (fun i ↦ scalarMu σ δ (k i ^ 2 - b i ^ 2))

lean_source.name: OAI.SharpLiebThirring.MatrixProof.fieldPrimitive_endpoint_limit
lean_source.text:
lemma fieldPrimitive_endpoint_limit {N : ℕ} {σ : ℝ} (hσ₀ : 0 < σ) (hσ₁ : σ < 1)
    (k : Fin N → ℝ) (hk : ∀ i, 0 ≤ k i) :
    Tendsto (fun δ : ℝ ↦ fieldPrimitive σ δ k (-diagonal k) - fieldPrimitive σ δ k (diagonal k))
      (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (∑ i, ∫ s in -(k i)..k i, (k i ^ 2 - s ^ 2) ^ σ))

lean_source.name: OAI.SharpLiebThirring.MatrixProof.hermitianField_state_jensen
lean_source.text:
lemma hermitianField_state_jensen {σ δ : ℝ} (hσ₀ : 0 < σ) (hσ₁ : σ < 1) (hδ : 0 < δ)
    (φ : Matrix n n ℂ →L[ℝ] ℝ) (hφ : ∀ A, A.PosSemidef → 0 ≤ φ A) (hφ₁ : φ 1 = 1)
    {C B : Matrix n n ℂ} (hC : C.IsHermitian) (hB : B.IsHermitian) :
    φ (hermitianField σ δ C B) ≤ scalarMu σ δ (φ C - (φ B) ^ 2)

lean_source.name: OAI.SharpLiebThirring.MatrixProof.rankone_hermitian_comparison
lean_source.kind: lemma (rank-one comparison, complex Hermitian, general C)
lean_source.text:
/-- The complete complex Hermitian rank-one comparison, before identifying the
real symmetric field with its complexification. -/
lemma rankone_hermitian_comparison {σ δ : ℝ} (hσ₀ : 0 < σ) (hσ₁ : σ < 1) (hδ : 0 < δ)
    {C B : Matrix n n ℂ} (hC : C.IsHermitian) (hB : B.IsHermitian) (a : n → ℂ)
    (hM : hermitianField σ δ C B = vecMulVec a (star a)) :
    (vectorMass a) ^ (1 + 1 / σ) ≤ (trace (vecMulVec a (star a) * (C - B ^ 2))).re

lean_source.name: OAI.SharpLiebThirring.MatrixProof.source_rankone_comparison
lean_source.text:
/-- The rank-one comparison for the real field
with its symmetric-cutoff definition. -/
theorem source_rankone_comparison {N : ℕ} {σ δ : ℝ} (hσ₀ : 0 < σ) (hσ₁ : σ < 1)
    (hδ : 0 < δ) (k : Fin N → ℝ) {B : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℝ} (hB : B.IsHermitian)
    (a : Fin N → ℝ) (hM : matrixField σ δ k B = vecMulVec a a) :
    (∑ i, a i ^ 2) ^ (1 + 1 / σ) ≤
      ∑ i, a i * ((diagonal (fun i ↦ k i ^ 2) - B ^ 2) *ᵥ a) i

open_problems.title: Sharp Lieb-Thirring on the half-line with a Hermitian Robin matrix (or Dirichlet) boundary condition for 1/2 < gamma < 3/2
open_problems.statement: For H = -d^2/dx^2 (x) I - V on L^2(R_+, C^N) with phi'(0) = S phi(0), find the sharp bound on Tr(H)_-^gamma in terms of int tr V^{gamma+1/2} (and S), 1/2 < gamma < 3/2.
open_problems.reference: Exner-Laptev-Usman, CMP 326 (2014), arXiv:1301.4986 (sharp results stated for the matrix semi-axis problem, range reported for gamma >= 3/2 / endpoint cases; not read in full); Schimmer, J. Spectral Theory (2022), arXiv:1912.13264 (improved non-sharp Robin/Dirichlet bounds via double commutation).
open_problems.status: open in the interval as far as found (WebSearch summaries only). Neumann (S = 0) is now a corollary of 262-S by even reflection with constant 2 L^(1)_{gamma,1}; Robin with S != 0 and Dirichlet are not.
open_problems.obstruction_match: Strongest structural match found. The calibration identity (J(B) + a^T B a)' produces the boundary term a(0)^T B(0) a(0); for Robin data the quadratic form has exactly the boundary term <phi(0), S phi(0)>, so the path should start at B(0) = S (a non-diagonal Hermitian matrix that need not commute with K) instead of at K. The Lean field and primitive are already defined and differentiable at every Hermitian B and for any Hermitian C (hermitianField, hermitianPotential_hasFDerivAt), so J(S) is available; for diagonal S, fieldPrimitive_diagonal gives it in closed form.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Replace the two-sided path K -> -K on a finite interval by a one-sided path S -> -K on [0, r]; redo the mod-2 continuation with a fixed initial value (the start is no longer a free endpoint, so the parity count changes); compute J(-K) - J(S); identify the extremal (likely a truncated soliton with matched log-derivative). Dirichlet corresponds to B(0) = +inf and needs a renormalized primitive (scalar mu is negative and linear for negative arguments, so the naive boundary term diverges).
open_problems.payoff: med (closes a named family of half-line problems; not a famous conjecture)
open_problems.difficulty: med-high (topology of the path step must be redone; the sharp form with S is not scale invariant and may not be one-bound-state type)

negative_controls.title: gamma < 1/2 in d = 1: no Lieb-Thirring inequality (proved false)
negative_controls.statement: For 0 < gamma < 1/2, optimalConstant gamma = top: with W = eps w, the ground state energy is about -(eps int w)^2/4, so |E|^gamma / int W^{gamma+1/2} ~ eps^{gamma-1/2} -> inf.
negative_controls.why_device_fails: sigma = gamma - 1/2 < 0: fieldNormalization is negative, mu(z) = (z+delta)^sigma - delta^sigma is decreasing, and the rank-one exponent 1 + 1/sigma is negative; every field lemma carries 0 < sigma.

negative_controls.title: gamma > 3/2: the one-bound-state constant is false (proved false)
negative_controls.statement: For gamma > 3/2, ENNReal.ofReal (sharpConstant gamma) < optimalConstant gamma, since L_{gamma,1} = L^cl_{gamma,1} > L^(1)_{gamma,1} (Lieb-Thirring 1976; Frank-Gontier-Lewin CMP 2021: never attained by finitely many eigenvalues for gamma > max(0, 2-d/2)).
negative_controls.why_device_fails: sigma >= 1: integral of (1+s^2)^{sigma-3/2} diverges; in Lean the Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is 0, so fieldNormalization = 0 and matrixField is identically 0. At sigma = 1 the naive field K^2 - B^2 is already a gradient (see S4), so the device is unnecessary there.

negative_controls.title: Non-self-adjoint (complex) potentials in 1D
negative_controls.statement: Lieb-Thirring-type bounds for complex V fail in the strong form (Boegli 2021, arXiv:2111.03938; Boegli-Stampach 2021; Boegli-Petpradittha-Stampach 2025, arXiv:2510.02192), per summaries.
negative_controls.why_device_fails: The field uses Hermitian functional calculus (cfc), trace gradients on selfAdjoint matrices and Klein-type monotonicity; none survive for non-normal pencils.

top5.target: O1: sharp half-line LT with Hermitian Robin matrix S (1/2 < gamma < 3/2)
top5.argument: Best structural match found. The calibration identity produces a boundary term a^T B a that matches the Robin form term exactly when the path starts at B(0) = S, and the Lean field, primitive and gradient are already defined for arbitrary Hermitian B and C, so the device is importable as is. Statable with about 150 new lines (half-line matrix H1 + Robin form). Measurement: prover budget for the one-sided action inequality with vs without MatrixOrder/FieldLimit/FieldPrimitive/BoundaryValues/RankOne. Risks: the sharp form is not scale invariant and is not known; the continuation (36% of the DAG, PL parity) must be redone for a fixed initial value; Neumann (S = 0) is only a corollary.

top5.target: S1: finite-matrix sharp LT at gamma = 1 (Read-Schulz) / on (1/2,3/2) (262-M)
top5.argument: Cleanest measurable library-value experiment: the field is reused verbatim and only C2 is new. Statable with about 120 lines of matrix Model.lean. It is an extension of the item's own theorem, so a speedup here does NOT confirm a jump; it calibrates how much the device library is worth to a prover. Comparing with Read-Schulz's different device (cumulative mass A(x)) at gamma = 1 is also an informal test of whether the field is the cheaper route.

Vector-valued half-line problem with a noncommuting vertex condition, so the field's noncommutative content is actually needed. Statable with about 120 lines. Low confidence: the potential is diagonal per edge, and odd N may reduce to O1 with a rank-one Robin S, in which case it merges with rank 1.

top5.target: O3: sharp Jacobi-matrix LT for 1/2 < gamma < 3/2
top5.argument: Statable now on finite sections. Included because it is the only open discrete target and is cheap to state; but the gauge-shift identity behind the field has no evident discrete analogue, so expect failure. Doubles as a negative-leaning control.

top5.target: N1/N2 + S2/S4 controls (gamma < 1/2 false; gamma > 3/2 one-state constant false; N = 1 Keller; sigma = 1 naive field)
top5.argument: All statable now with Model.lean. They bracket the device: it is defined exactly on 0 < sigma < 1, the range where the theorem holds, collapses to the classical calibration at N = 1, and is superfluous at sigma = 1. A speedup harness that reports gains on these is miscalibrated.

verdict_part_b: No strong device-reuse speedup target on a known theorem was found. Every known theorem the item reaches (Read-Schulz gamma = 1, endpoints 1/2 and 3/2, matrix versions, Neumann half-line, even star graphs, higher-d constants via lifting) is reached through the THEOREM or its same-family extension, not through the device. The device is tied to second-order 1D problems with 0 < sigma < 1 (it degenerates at both endpoints and has no evident discrete, higher-order or d-dimensional analogue). The only plausible device-reuse candidates are open half-line/graph problems (O1, O2) where a noncommuting boundary matrix enters, with low-medium confidence.

precedent_check.earlier_equivalent_found: none. Read-Schulz full text VERIFIED 2026-10-12 (v1 + v2; see novelty.json verified_checks). Its matrix device is the explicit cumulative mass A(x) plus a midpoint Schur-multiplier lift B = sum c_rl A^r Q A^l of a fixed tangent function. It is K-free, linear in the density, a flux rather than a gradient, and not M_delta at sigma = 1/2. RS also has no Laptev-Weidl or phase-space matrix device. Other neighbours as in novelty.json: Laptev-Weidl phase-space integral (ingredient without the B-shift) and Benguria-Loss 2000/2004 (template). A search for f(K^2 - 2sB + s^2)-type trace-gradient fields returned unrelated Riccati trace bounds and one 2026 covariance-estimation paper (arXiv:2608.20223) that uses a trace-gradient flow but no pencil integral or calibration (summary only).
precedent_check.downgrade: No downgrade from this pass. The main risk (an expert identifying M_delta as a known local Weyl density of a gauge-shifted operator used as a calibration) is unresolved.

No other family in the release (CONTENTS.md, preprint grep, OAI Lean grep) uses the field or LiebThirring declarations; other Lieb-Thirring mentions are Araki-Lieb-Thirring trace inequalities or LT used as a black box (Coulomb families).
